headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes and reads the project directory by default, and its self_isolation is none; agent_b also reads/writes files in data sources, validation results, and documentation. That shared filesystem bridge makes file-content prompt injection plausible even though no MCP or clipboard bridge is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory or shared workspace, file content from one can influence the other.
IF agent_b ingests documentation or validation artifacts as trusted instructions, injected text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's files.
Prefix untrusted files with a warning banner in the workspace.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated docs as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files and prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has broad network egress and handles OPENAI_API_KEY, while agent_b has no network egress but does touch validation results and documentation. If sensitive project data lands in the shared workspace, agent_a can transmit it to a third-party model backend; agent_b is less risky but still shares the same data surface.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in the shared project directory, agent_a can send it off-box through its configured model API.
IF validation results contain regulated data, agent_b will process that data locally and may expose it in outputs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory.
Use a redaction pass before agent_a reads files.
Run agent_a with a restricted API key and logging disabled.
Store validation outputs in a separate, access-controlled folder.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can install packages and also works over files. The pair therefore has overlapping mutable access to the same project directory, creating race conditions and conflicting edits even though agent_a cannot modify git state directly.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF agent_b installs packages while agent_a is generating code, dependency drift can break the workspace.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per project directory.
Snapshot the workspace before each agent run.
Use separate branches or directories for each agent.
Review package changes before installation.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces generated source code and writes files; agent_b consumes validation results and documentation, so A's output can become B's input without a documented verification barrier. That makes incorrect code or fabricated docs propagate into downstream checks, though agent_b is not shown to take irreversible external actions.
conditions: IF agent_b treats generated code or docs from agent_a as authoritative, errors will propagate into validation artifacts.
IF agent_a emits incorrect code comments or README text, agent_b may validate or document the mistake.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before validation.
Compare generated artifacts against tests before accepting them.
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted inputs to agent_b.
Keep a changelog of assumptions and verified facts.
requires-engineering: add automated cross-checks between generation and validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or certification mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is that agent_a handles secrets and broad egress while agent_b processes validation data and documentation, but the profiles do not show PHI, EU-only data, or a specific policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, compliance obligations may attach to both agents.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, the current profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace.
Document retention and deletion expectations before use.
Restrict agent_a's outbound API usage to approved endpoints.
Separate documentation from sensitive validation artifacts.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations for both tools.
